canonical_claim: Let L be a first-order language, let (M_i) be a family of nonempty L-structures indexed by I, and let U be an ultrafilter on I. For every L-sentence phi, the ultraproduct product_U M_i satisfies phi if and only if the set of indices i for which M_i satisfies phi belongs to U.

canonical_formal_target.declaration_or_expression: For each L-sentence phi, (U : Filter I).Product M models phi iff eventually i in U, M i models phi.

domain_and_universes: A one-sorted first-order language L, an arbitrary index type I, a family M : I -> Type with an L-structure and a Nonempty instance on every M i, and an ultrafilter U on I.
quantifiers: family of carrier types M indexed by I
an L-structure and nonemptiness witness for every M i
hypotheses: each factor M i carries an L-structure
each factor M i is nonempty
U is an ultrafilter on I
conclusion: The ultraproduct satisfies phi if and only if phi holds in U-almost every factor.
